item.title: Brighton cruise past Arsenal to end the champions perfect start
item.description: Brighton secure a 3-0 victory over Premier League champions Arsenal to inflict the Gunners first defeat of the season, as the hosts celebrate their 125th anniversary.

item.title: Newcastle hold off Hull to seal win at St. James' Park
item.description: Newcastle United hold off a late Hull City fightback to seal a narrow 2-1 win, putting an end to the Tigers unbeaten start to the Premier League season.

item.title: Everton's unbeaten run continues with win over 10-man Ipswich
item.description: Unbeaten Everton move up to fifth in the Premier League, with Thierno Barry's goal making the difference against 10-man Ipswich Town.

item.title: Spurs lose again as Villa hold on for first league win
item.description: Aston Villa pick up their first win of the Premier League season after five matches, holding off a late push from a Tottenham Hotspur side who remain without a win in the league.

item.title: Brentford stay unbeaten as they put three past Chelsea
item.description: Brentford maintain their unbeaten start in the Premier League as they score three second-half goals to beat Chelsea 3-0 at the Gtech Community Stadium.

item.title: Brighton humbling 'a big lesson' for Arsenal - Arteta
item.description: An uncharacteristic performance from Arsenal saw the Gunners ship three goals in the defeat to Brighton - but could the loss be the "big lesson" they needed?

item.title: From near oblivion to Europe - Brighton celebrate 125th anniversary in style
item.description: From obscurity and near oblivion to Premier League and Europe - Brighton celebrate their 125th anniversary.

item.title: No revival in sight for 'fragile' Spurs after Villa defeat
item.description: Tottenham look no closer to solving their problems as they slip to a home defeat by Aston Villa to add to their Premier League misery.

item.title: Ratcliffe 'must go' says Man Utd Muslim fan group
item.description: The Manchester United Muslim Supporters Club says United co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe "must go" after he spoke out against immigration and said the country was "on the slide".

item.title: Castellanos spitting claim overshadows West Ham's show of character
item.description: Millwall keeper Filip Marshcall alleges he was spat at by West Ham forward Taty Castellanos during their 2-2 draw.

item.title: Suzuki proves worthy replacement for Martinez at Villa
item.description: Aston Villa new boy Zion Suzuki deserves as much credit as anyone for their first Premier League win of the season at struggling Tottenham.

item.title: Clark resigns as Hartlepool boss in post-match interview
item.description: Lee Clark resigns as Hartlepool United head coach after a sixth loss in seven games following the 3-1 home defeat by Worthing.

item.title: Lowly Peterborough sack manager Williams
item.description: Peterborough United sack manager Luke Williams after Saturday's defeat at home by Doncaster leaves them second from bottom in League One.

item.title: 'It's a big lesson to learn' - Arteta on 'painful' Brighton defeat
item.description: Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta says Arsenal were "very far" from the standards required to compete after the Gunners lost 3-0 to Brighton - their first defeat in the Premier League this season.

item.title: Malard scores on debut as Chelsea beat Birmingham
item.description: Melvine Malard scores on her WSL debut for Chelsea as the Blues run out as comfortable winners against Birmingham City at Stamford Bridge.

item.title: 'Stay humble' - Hurzeler's plea to Brighton after huge Arsenal win
item.description: Brighton manager Fabian Hurzeler highlights his team's intensity, togetherness and squad depth following their resounding 3-0 win against Arsenal in the Premier League.

item.title: Tottenham need 'blood & fight' not just to play better - de Zerbi
item.description: Spurs head coach Roberto de Zerbi says his side "have to be stronger" following their loss against Aston Villa in the Premier League, focusing on the squad's "behaviour" rather than their quality.

item.title: Goodwin double helps London City win at struggling Charlton
item.description: London City Lionesses earn their first away win of the season, with Isobel Goodwin scoring twice, as they emphatically beat a struggling Charlton side who have now lost all three of their WSL games.

item.title: Why the Black Country derby means so much to Wolves and West Brom
item.description: Wolves and West Bromwich Albion meet for the first time in a Black Country derby for the first time in the league since May 2021.

item.title: Emery praises Jackson & Suzuki after 'fantastic' win at Spurs
item.description: Aston Villa manager Unai Emery admires his side's resilience in their 3-2 away victory against Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League, highlighting the performances of striker Nicolas Jackson and goalkeeper Zion Suzuki.

item.title: 100 years on, is time up for Milan's iconic San Siro?
item.description: As the iconic home of AC Milan and Inter Milan turns 100, BBC Sport visits the San Siro - the venue for the recent Winter Olympics opening ceremony, to find out why that could have been the last global event held at the stadium, and what comes next.

item.title: Learning English, finding connections - Putellas settles at London City
item.description: BBC Sport's Alex Scott, Fara Williams and Anita Asante speak to London City Lionesses star Alexia Putellas, to discuss the 4-1 win at Charlton and how she is settling at her new club.

item.title: Kane makes history and Olise nets hat-trick as Bayern thrash Union Berlin
item.description: HHarry Kane makes history by becoming the fastest player to reach 100 Bundesliga goals in his 98th game, while Michael Olise nets a hat-trick as Bayern Munich thrash Union Berlin 7-0.

item.title: Man City strike late to beat Liverpool and maintain perfect start
item.description: Man City come out on top of a thrilling WSL encounter against Liverpool, requiring two goals in the closing stages of the game to seal a 4-2 win, their third victory in three league fixtures so far this season.

item.title: 'We're unpredictable' - Andrews delighted with 'brilliant' Brentford
item.description: Brentford manager Keith Andrews is full of praise after a resounding 3-0 win against West London rivals Chelsea, branding them "brilliant" following a unbeaten start to the Premier League campaign.

item.title: Chelsea miss Joao Pedro... and can't stop conceding goals
item.description: Chelsea's problem was defending, but with Joao Pedro ruled out through injury, scoring goals has also become an issue.

item.title: Arsenal open to Dowman loan in right circumstances
item.description: Arsenal are open to allowing teenage prodigy Max Dowman to leave the club on loan this term if it aids his development.

item.title: Gabriel, 15, in Barcelona amid speculation over future
item.description: Man Utd youngster JJ Gabriel travels to Barcelona as some of Europe's biggest clubs continue to vie for his signature.

item.title: Flex your football brain with our daily quizzes
item.description: Test your ball knowledge against today's Who Am I?, Five in Five and Brainteaser.

item.title: Sutton's predictions v legendary guitarist Johnny Marr
item.description: BBC Sport football expert Chris Sutton takes on legendary guitarist and Man City fan Johnny Marr, plus the BBC readers and AI with his predictions for this weekend's Premier League fixtures.

item.title: Will England boss Tuchel 'embrace the chaos'?
item.description: After the World Cup, England boss Thomas Tuchel wanted greater control. Two months on, he is keen to "embrace the chaos" after naming his squad for the upcoming Nations League fixtures.

item.title: London City's new training centre 'better than most Premier League clubs' - Kang
item.description: Michele Kang believes London City Lionesses' planned new training ground will set a new standard in the women's game and surpass facilities used by most men's Premier League clubs.

item.title: Uefa & Concacaf demand Fifa pays $10m to all 211 members
item.description: Uefa and Concacaf issue a joint statement calling on Fifa to pay $10m from its cash reserves to each of the 211 member associations.

item.title: Poor imitation of Ange team - where do Celtic & O'Neill go from here?
item.description: After another defeat, keeping the faith is surely becoming more testing for Celtic's fans, writes Tom English.

item.title: How Iraola is moving Liverpool on from the Slot era
item.description: BBC Sport looks at how new manager Andoni Iraola is moving Liverpool on from the Arne Slot era after their disappointing form last season.

item.title: Nottingham Forest stadium expansion approved - so what now?
item.description: Will the dream of a bigger City Ground finally become a reality?

item.title: Oxford apologise for United 93 shirt advert
item.description: Oxford United apologises for the image, which features the call sign of one of the planes used in the 9/11 attacks.

item.title: How to follow the Premier League on the BBC this weekend
item.description: Our Ask Me Anything team explains how to follow matches from week five of the Premier League season on the BBC this weekend.

item.title: A team that offered hope... then, four months later, Hamas attacked Israel
item.description: Can the potential of a golden generation of Israel's footballers, in sport and society, be realised?

item.title: Why dealing with defeat is key for Lampard at Coventry
item.description: BBC Sport columnist Tony Pulis explains why Coventry boss Frank Lampard needs to manage himself as well as his players after their poor start to the season.

item.title: Ranking the greatest all-time fantasy football icons
item.description: There's nothing quite like the satisfaction of unearthing an absolute Fantasy Premier League bargain - so who are the most iconic picks ever?

item.title: 'Superstar' Dowman shows his class - but Arsenal know caution is needed
item.description: Max Dowman shines with two goals against Ipswich Town - but boss Mikel Arteta warns Arsenal cannot rush his development.

item.title: Manager ins and outs - 2026-27
item.description: BBC Sport tracks all the manager ins and outs in the Premier League, Scottish Premiership, Women's Super League, English Football League and National League.

item.title: All done deals in September 2026
item.description: Check out the significant signings and departures in the Premier League, Scottish Premiership, EFL and Women's Super League.

item.title: What are the Premier League rules for academy players?
item.description: BBC Sport's Ask Me Anything team looks at what rules players and clubs must follow when teenagers play in the Premier League

item.title: What is the Premier League's KMI Panel and how does it work?
item.description: The Premier League introduced its Key Match Incident (KMI) Panel four years ago

item.title: Why have the Premier League announced Christmas fixtures early?
item.description: BBC Sport's Ask Me Anything team explain why this season's Christmas fixtures have been announced more than a month earlier than scheduled

item.title: Why is Sunderland vs Arsenal at 8pm on Saturday?
item.description: BBC Sport's Ask Me Anything team explains why Saturday's Premier League fixture between Sunderland and Arsenal is kicking off at 8pm

item.title: Why do Tottenham Hotspur not have a stadium sponsor?
item.description: BBC Sport's Ask Me Anything team explains why after more than seven years, Tottenham Hotspur are yet to agree a stadium sponsorship deal.

item.title: How does prize money work in the EFL Cup?
item.description: BBC Sport's Ask Me Anything team explains how prize money works in the EFL Cup

item.title: Criticism 'normal' after poor start - Man Utd's Olid
item.description: Manchester United manager Eva Olid says it is "normal" to expect "constructive criticism" following their poor start to the WSL campaign.

item.title: Sorensen to join Republic of Ireland coaching staff
item.description: Former Everton manager Brian Sorensen is set to join the Republic of Ireland squad for their Women's World Cup play-off qualifiers this year.

item.title: Arsenal had more than 20 players on shortlist to capitalise on title win
item.description: Senior football correspondent Sami Mokbel goes inside Arsenal's bid to capitalise on their Premier League title and strengthen their squad this summer.

item.title: 73 goals from dropping deep - we ask Kane to break down how he did it
item.description: Harry Kane was the highest goalscorer in Europe last season, yet he plays like a midfielder. We ask him to break down his game.

item.title: Life as a Wag in the transfer window
item.description: What is life like for footballers' families during the transfer window where a last-minute deal means you need to uproot your life and move hundreds of miles?

item.title: A secret invite and other 'pinch-me' moments before Leicester woke up
item.description: Leicester are gearing up for League One but 10 years ago they were defending Premier League champions. The dream moments haven't been forgotten.

item.title: The summer that changed Welsh football
item.description: A decade on from Euro 2016, key figures tell BBC Sport Wales the inside story of the summer that changed Welsh football forever.

item.title: The country that doesn't play football... yet
item.description: Nauru is the only nation to have never played an official international football match and hardly anyone there plays the game. Is that about to change?

item.title: In spotlight but shunning limelight - Olise's unique rise to top
item.description: A footballer who dislikes too much media attention, but Michael Olise might not have much choice if he carries on his World Cup heroics.
